newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech FinMin sees tender adviser soon - CTK.
newsitem.headline: Czech FinMin sees tender adviser soon - CTK.

text.p: The Finance Ministry should choose an adviser for a tender to sell the state's roughly one-third holding in the fourth largest Czech bank, IPB a.s., in the coming days, the CTK news agency reported on Tuesday.
The agency, quoting Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik, said the name of the adviser would be made public following the closing of a mandate contract, which "is a matter of days".
Earlier this month Kocarnik said conditions for the tender would be announced by the end of January.
A special committee has been formed at the Finance Ministry to prepare the sale, which is expected to be geared toward choosing a strong foreign partner.

A key economic aide to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, Martin Kocourek, said in November that Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) was seeking to be the arranger for the IPB selloff. Other firms seeking the mandate, if any, have not been revealed.
The government holds a 31.5 percent stake in IPB through its National Property Fund (NPF), and another roughly six percent through the postal service Ceska Posta.

The exact amount of shares to be offered in the tender has not been released. NPF chairman Roman Ceska, who does not have a seat in the cabinet which must ultimately approve the sale, has said that Japanese investment bank Nomura has the "best chance" to win the tender.
He also said however that he hoped the selection process would be transparent. The tender should take about six months to complete.

Apart from Nomura, the Dutch concerns ING Groep NV and ABN AMRO have also been touted by Czech media as parties interested in taking a stake in IPB, although both have refused to comment on the matter.
